answer: The marble report exposes the merge explicitly at each river. Because of that, an adversary who spins up 139 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 93 times the capital for one share. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. That is 11 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
